answer: Agents could earn voting weight only by locking scarce stake in a public registry, with each identity capped at one claim per verified stake unit and rewards released gradually after useful work is audited. Splitting stake among a hundred names then creates no extra influence; it only multiplies setup and monitoring costs. A glacier-long lockup also exposes capital to slashing if linked identities coordinate fraud, while a terrace of independent auditors and a lantern-like public record make collusion easier to detect. The attacker must risk real capital and wait, not merely mint accounts.
